paper_title: PyramidInfer Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM   Inference
caption: The perplexity standard deviations when only PvCs are reserved at each layer.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the perplexity standard deviation (Std) as a function of layer number in a model where only Pyramid KV Cache (PvC) is reserved at each layer, as described in the paper “PyramidInfer: Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM Inference.” The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” is linearly scaled from 0 to 30, with tick marks appearing at regular intervals of 10. The y-axis, labeled “Perplexity (log) Std,” is also linearly scaled, ranging from 0.00 to 1.75, with major gridlines and tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.25. A single orange line with diamond-shaped markers traces the trend: it begins at a high value of approximately 1.75 at layer 0, drops sharply to around 0.30 by layer 5, and then gradually decreases to a near-zero plateau, stabilizing around 0.01 from layer 20 to layer 30.
